hook: Go in expecting a cosmic horror monster and you get the wrong article in the best way. SCP-2662 is a towering, tentacled being whose biggest problem is that people keep worshipping it. Content note: the incident logs include masturbation and group sex as ritual, self-stabbing, the mutilation and killing of a piglet, and cannibalism, all played for exasperated comedy.
whyItMatters: The file takes an eldritch template and turns it into a sitcom in which the god is the only reasonable person in the room. The kindness tag fits, since the horror lives entirely in the human followers while the entity mostly wants its newspaper and a monthly budget for video games. Its containment is voluntary, and that detail quietly carries the whole premise.
thingsToNotice:
The comedy comes from friction between the dry timestamped log and the entity's complaints: cultists blast up through the floor, stab their hands, masturbate and paint symbols with the mix of blood and fluids while it protests that it just showered; a fake researcher castrates a piglet, slits its throat over the breakfast newspaper, and is then shot and eaten by her fellow impostors while the entity throws up in the toilet.

The last incident is the turn that earns the Keter rating. While the task force is called away to a mission that turns out not to exist, two members left behind lock up their colleagues, bring in a truckload of D-class, carve symbols into their buttocks and thighs and start an orgy, and when the entity yells at them to stop, they all freeze: its control over followers is maturing. The cultists tell it the Foundation will never let it leave just for asking, and its offhand answer, that it can simply wait until it is strong enough to break out, reframes the whole file as a countdown before it goes back to sit in the shower.
